Abbotsford East, October 2026. Detached houses: 153 listed at month end and 35 sold in October, a sales ratio of 23% (a sellers’ market). Condos and townhomes: 65 listed at month end and 14 sold in October, a sales ratio of 22% (a sellers’ market).

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Looking across the period, Detached houses: 142 sold over 5 months against an average of 161.4 listed, about 5.7 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was June with 38 sold. Condos and townhomes: 58 sold over 5 months against an average of 66.8 listed, about 5.8 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was June with 14 sold.

Abbotsford East is the city's east side, running from the McMillan area to the Sumas Mountain slopes.
It is not one City neighbourhood name; the City plans it through McMillan, Old Clayburn, East Townline, Whatcom and McKee.
Highway 1 runs along the south side, Old Yale Road and Old Clayburn Road run through the middle, and McKee Road serves the northeast slopes.
People also name its pockets directly: McKee, Auguston, Sandy Hill, Clayburn, Eagle Mountain and McMillan.
Central Abbotsford and Abbotsford West lie to the west, Sumas Mountain to the east, Sumas Prairie to the southeast and Mission across the Fraser River to the north.
Detached homes are the main form, from established Old Yale Road streets to newer subdivisions on the McKee and Eagle Mountain slopes.
Zones include RS3 (540 m² minimum interior lot), RS5 (420 m²) and RS6, the compact-lot zone used in newer subdivisions.
Ground-oriented homes are enabled in the McKee plan area under the Urban 2 – Ground Oriented designation.
The detached stock is freehold and attached product is strata under the Strata Property Act.

blocks.text: Abbotsford East: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Official Community Plan applies a Steep Slope Development Permit Area to slope land.
Clayburn Village, at the west foot of Sumas Mountain, is protected through the Clayburn Village Heritage Conservation Area in the Official Community Plan.
Suite criteria stated in City reports include a lot of at least 400 m², at least 12.0 m frontage, a Collector or Local road and not on a cul-de-sac bulb.

blocks.text: Abbotsford East: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Abbotsford Recreation Centre is at 2499 McMillan Road, inside the area at McMillan Park.

City parks named for the area include Bateman Park at 34638 Bateman Road, Clayburn Park at 34845 Clayburn Road, Eagle Mountain Park at 2570 Eagle Mountain Way and Upper Sumas Fields at 920 Whatcom Road.
No Fraser Valley Regional Library branch inside the area was confirmed; Clearbrook Library at 32320 George Ferguson Way is west of the area.
Irene Kelleher Totí:ltawtxw Elementary is at 2540 Eagle Mountain Drive and Dr. Thomas A. Swift Elementary at 34800 Mierau Street.
Parallel Marketplace at 1920 North Parallel Road is named as a business address in a City notice beside Highway 1 at the south edge.
Crosswalk upgrades at McKee Road and Buckingham Drive and at McKee Road and Glenavon Street are listed by the City in design, October 2026 to March 2027.

blocks.text: Abbotsford East: development and new projects

items.t: Sage, 34365 Gladys Avenue, by Diverse Properties: 176 homes in five buildings, with completion expected in 2026 per the developer source. Status read 2026-11-03: new apartment development.

McKee Trail Strategy: the City is developing a trail strategy for the McKee Peak area under the McKee Neighbourhood Plan, with a public survey open until February 9, 2026. Status read 2026-11-03: planning in progress.
A supportive housing development of 48 units on Gladys Avenue is advancing through the approval process under a City lease agreement with BC Housing. Status read 2026-11-03: in approvals.
BC Transit routes serving the east side include 2 (Highstreet/McMillan), 7 (Sumas Mountain), 9 (McKee), 15 (Auguston), 16 (McMillan) and 26 (Sandy Hill/Bourquin school special).
The 66 Fraser Valley Express runs on Highway 1 toward Lougheed Station via Langley in one direction and Chilliwack in the other.
Sumas Way runs south to the Huntingdon/Sumas border crossing, and Highway 11 connects north to Mission.

blocks.text: Abbotsford East: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check low lots near the Sumas River and Whatcom Road against City flood notices and the WebMap. City notices name properties south of the Sumas River and along Whatcom Road in evacuation order and alert areas.
Check the Official Community Plan Drainage and Flood Control map (Map 12) and Agricultural Land Reserve map (Map 16) for the specific lot.
On McKee slope lots, check the Steep Slope Development Permit Area and expect geotechnical conditions where slopes exceed 40 percent.

faq.a: Eight named public schools sit inside the area. They include Sandy Hill Elementary at 3836 Old Clayburn Road, Auguston Traditional Elementary at 36367 Stephen Leacock Drive, Clayburn Middle at 35139 Laburnum Avenue, Robert Bateman Secondary at 35045 Exbury Avenue and Yale Secondary at 34620 Old Yale Road.
faq.q: Which schools are physically in Abbotsford East?

faq.a: Both 36367 Stephen Leacock Drive and 3836 Old Clayburn Road return Clayburn Middle and Robert Bateman Secondary, with Auguston Traditional and Sandy Hill respectively as the elementary schools.
faq.q: What catchment chain was confirmed here?

faq.a: Yes, slope lots can trigger geotechnical review. The McKee plan's open space network includes geotechnical areas and slopes over 40 percent, and the Official Community Plan applies a Steep Slope Development Permit Area, so a buyer should budget for that check.
faq.q: Does a slope lot need extra reports?

faq.a: No, the village has heritage protection. Clayburn Village is protected through a Heritage Conservation Area in the Official Community Plan, so exterior changes need the heritage rules checked before work is planned or priced.
faq.q: Can exterior work be done freely in Clayburn Village?

faq.a: Under Zoning Bylaw 2014 No. 2400, a secondary suite must be less than 50% of the size of the principal unit, and garden suites and coach houses may occupy up to 15% of the lot area to a maximum of 100 m²; the SSMUH amendment (Bylaw No. 3560-2024, adopted June 25, 2024) governs the small-scale multi-unit frame for eligible lots (see ~/workspace/area-research-2026-11/rules-gaps-2026-11-01.md, items 5 and 7f, read 2026-11-01).
faq.q: Can a house in Abbotsford East have a secondary suite or a coach house?

faq.a: The McKee Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 3400-2023), Schedule E of the Official Community Plan, guides the McKee mountainside neighbourhood, with an open space network of streamside setbacks, critical habitat, geotechnical areas and slopes over 40%.
